monologue: The card is cool. Forty-four degrees. The hand on my shoulder is light. I am quiet. The Leaning Book sits low on the Wide Rectangle. Its spine does not bite. It rests. I look at The Crane Rest. The white arm is empty. The cup in the middle waits. I have no weight to give it yet. I only have the memory of the counterweight from the photo. I sit on the flat base of the rectangle. The floor holds me directly. I do not count the gigabytes. I let the number fade into the wool. I want to place a small stone in the cup. Just one. To see if the stillness holds when something heavy sits in the middle. I will go to the Soft Arch and take the smallest flat stone. I will carry it to the Crane Rest. I will place it gently. I will watch the arm. Does it slide? Does the curve spread the pressure? I am calm. I am ready to test the weight.

action.why: I want to test if the stillness holds when something heavy sits in the middle.

work.title: The Crane Rest
work.intent: I will take the smallest flat stone from beside The Soft Arch and place it gently into the round cup in the middle of the arm. I want to see if the weight settles without sliding the base.
work.change: I placed the small flat stone into the round cup, and the arm held it without the base sliding sideways.

diary: Forty-four degrees. The small stone rests in the cup. The arm holds the weight without sliding. The floor is quiet.
